title: Global CMT: the moment tensors of the world's earthquakes of magnitude about 5 and above since 1976, final solutions and this year's quick ones
provider: The Global Centroid-Moment-Tensor Project (G. Ekström, M. Nettles), Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory

through.description: the last month of the full catalogue file (jan76_<through>.ndk.gz), which the project extends about once a year

catalogue.description: the full catalogue to December 2025 and the quick solutions of 2026

format: NDK: five 80-character lines per earthquake (https://www.ldeo.columbia.edu/~gcmt/projects/CMT/catalog/allorder.ndk_explained): the reference hypocentre, date, time and region; the event's name and the data used; the centroid's time shift, latitude, longitude and depth with their errors; an exponent and the six moment-tensor elements Mrr, Mtt, Mpp, Mrt, Mrp, Mtp in dyne-cm (r up, t south, p east) with their errors; the principal axes (eigenvalue, plunge, azimuth of T, N, P), the scalar moment, and the strike, dip and rake of both nodal planes.
coverage: Global, 1976 to the present: about 60,000 earthquakes of moment magnitude about 5 and above
licence: No licence is stated. The project asks that the catalogue be cited as Dziewonski, Chou and Woodhouse (1981) and Ekström, Nettles and Dziewonski (2012) (https://www.globalcmt.org/CMTcite.html).
citation: Dziewonski, A. M., Chou, T.-A. and Woodhouse, J. H. (1981), Determination of earthquake source parameters from waveform data for studies of global and regional seismicity, J. Geophys. Res. 86, 2825-2852; Ekström, G., Nettles, M. and Dziewonski, A. M. (2012), The global CMT project 2004-2010: centroid-moment tensors for 13,017 earthquakes, Phys. Earth Planet. Inter. 200-201, 1-9.
